configuration.calibration: expected calibration error over 10 confidence bins

criteria.gain: balanced accuracy favours the smoother, and neither log loss nor calibration error favours the online filter
criteria.no gain: balanced accuracy is negligible or favours the online filter, and log loss is negligible or favours the online filter
criteria.not_online: every difference is a smoothing gain: the smoother reads up to its lag after each window and reports that long after it, so no difference is an improvement of the online filter
criteria.primary: each smoother against the online filter on the same windows; every estimand is primary and read by the same rule
criteria.probability gain: balanced accuracy does not favour the smoother, log loss does, and neither balanced accuracy nor calibration error favours the online filter
criteria.trade-off: balanced accuracy favours the smoother, and log loss or calibration error favours the online filter
criteria.verdicts: favours model: mean >= delta and lower bound > 0; favours reference: mean <= -delta and upper bound < 0; negligible: the whole interval within (-delta, delta); uncertain: anything else

formulation.channels: hurdle, fitted per fold on the training households as in the Phase 3.3 follow-up
formulation.emissions: default_emissions of the household registry, pooled per channel
formulation.fitted: the population hurdle parameters, per fold, on the fold's training households' labelled windows only
formulation.prediction: most probable state of the posterior; no abstention
formulation.prior: stationary distribution of the default ontology, one step before the first window of the recording
formulation.transition: default StateOntology, time-homogeneous, one step per window
formulation.why: it is the recursion over every window with a pre-specified success on develop (Phase 3.3 follow-up, FR); partial pooling in the recursion was inconclusive (Phase 3.4, P2), and the Phase 3.1 time prior was evaluated only on declared information sets, never as a recursion
formulation.windows: every window of the recording, each channel's current count

households.use: each household is held out once; its fold's training households fit the channel models

configuration.inference: the online filter reads no window after the scored one; each smoother reads up to its lag after it and reports that long after it; the record states the longest lag, which bounds every estimate in it, and labels every cell and comparison with its own regime

lags.smoother: smooth_beliefs through regime_beliefs: each window's filtered belief revised with the filtered beliefs of up to lag later windows and the transition, starting every correction from the filtered belief at its horizon
lags.why: a small set declared before scoring and never searched: short, medium and long delays with an operational use each; lags beyond an hour serve only offline analysis and are not scored

operational.by_state: the same shares within the scored windows whose labelled state is each focus state
operational.changed: Share of a household's scored windows whose most probable state under the smoother differs from the online filter's.
operational.corrected: Share of a household's scored windows where the online filter's most probable state is wrong that the smoother gets right.
operational.corrections_among_changes: Share of a household's changed windows where the smoother is right and the online filter wrong.

operational.summary: one value per household; the mean and the median across households with household bootstrap intervals; no verdict

per_state_recall.rare_rule: share of labelled time below 0.05 in either fold's training households

lag_1.label: fixed-lag smoother, lag 1 window (5 min)
lag_1.role: short: one window, for a display that may run one window behind

lag_12.label: fixed-lag smoother, lag 12 windows (60 min)
lag_12.role: long: one hour, for retrospective hourly or daily reporting; the longest delay treated as plausible for a decision made the same day

lag_6.label: fixed-lag smoother, lag 6 windows (30 min)

online.label: online filter

configuration.reproduction: the online filter is also scored on every labelled window, as filter_hurdle@R, to reproduce the Phase 3.3 follow-up
configuration.scored_windows: each held-out household's labelled windows except the last 12 of its recording, identical for every regime, so every smoothed estimate reads its full lag

transitions.boundary_accuracy: Share of a household's scored windows within boundary_windows of a transition, before or after it, whose most probable state is right.
transitions.comparisons: boundary accuracy, and each group's detection rate and decision delay, as paired household differences against the online filter, read with the verdicts
transitions.decision_delay_minutes: The median over a household's detected transitions of the time from the transition to the moment the regime can first report the new state: the windows until its most probable state first equals the new state, plus its lag, times the step. Lower is better.
transitions.detection_rate: Share of a household's transitions after which the regime reports the new state at some window of the new episode.
transitions.group_rule: all transitions, and the transitions into each focus state
transitions.interior_accuracy: The same, for the scored windows further from every transition.
transitions.transition: A scored window whose labelled state differs from the labelled state of the window before it. Its episode runs while the following windows keep that labelled state, up to the last scored window; an unlabelled window ends it.

configuration.tuning: none: the lags, the boundary and the focus states are declared; nothing is fitted on held-out households

inference.provenance: declared by the experiment that wrote the record

metric_definitions.abstention_rate: Fraction of estimates that declined to name a state, because confidence or sensor coverage fell below threshold.
metric_definitions.accuracy: Fraction of scored estimates whose reported state equals the true state. A reported UNKNOWN is never correct, so abstentions count as errors.
metric_definitions.balanced_accuracy: Unweighted mean of per-class recall. Used in preference to accuracy because the states are heavily imbalanced and a model that always predicts the majority state scores highly on raw accuracy.
metric_definitions.boundary_accuracy: Share of a household's scored windows within boundary_windows of a transition, before or after it, whose most probable state is right.
metric_definitions.brier: Multiclass Brier score over the full posterior, in [0, 2]. A proper scoring rule; lower is better.
metric_definitions.broken: Share of a household's scored windows where the online filter's most probable state is right that the smoother gets wrong.
metric_definitions.calibration_error: Expected calibration error: the bin-weighted gap between stated confidence and observed accuracy. Answers whether a confidence of 0.9 means anything.
metric_definitions.changed: Share of a household's scored windows whose most probable state under the smoother differs from the online filter's.
metric_definitions.confusion: Counts of labelled true state (rows) against reported state (columns). The final column is UNKNOWN, so abstentions stay visible.
metric_definitions.confusion_summed: Sum of the per-household confusion matrices. Descriptive only; no comparison is computed from it.
metric_definitions.corrected: Share of a household's scored windows where the online filter's most probable state is wrong that the smoother gets right.
metric_definitions.corrections_among_changes: Share of a household's changed windows where the smoother is right and the online filter wrong.
metric_definitions.decision_delay_minutes: The median over a household's detected transitions of the time from the transition to the moment the regime can first report the new state: the windows until its most probable state first equals the new state, plus its lag, times the step. Lower is better.
metric_definitions.detection_rate: Share of a household's transitions after which the regime reports the new state at some window of the new episode.
metric_definitions.differences: The improvement in each paired held-out household.
metric_definitions.effect_size: Cohen's dz of the household improvements; null with one household or when every household improved by the same amount.
metric_definitions.excluded: Held-out households lacking a value from either model.
metric_definitions.favours_model, favours_reference, tied: Households where the model did better, worse, or exactly as well as the reference, with their proportions.
metric_definitions.household_summary: Mean, median, standard deviation, minimum and maximum of a metric across held-out households, each household counted once however many timestamps it has. Households without a value are listed as missing, not counted as zero. Observations are never pooled across households.
metric_definitions.improvement: Per-household paired difference oriented so that a positive value favours the model over the reference: model minus reference where higher is better, reference minus model where lower is better.
metric_definitions.interior_accuracy: The same, for the scored windows further from every transition.
metric_definitions.interval: Bootstrap interval resampling households, never timestamps, with the same resamples for the mean and the median. The method is percentile or BCa. BCa falls back to percentile where it is undefined, and the note says so.
metric_definitions.log_loss: Mean negative log probability assigned to the true state. Punishes confident errors far more than hedged ones.
metric_definitions.macro_f1: Unweighted mean F1 across the classes present in the truth.
metric_definitions.mean, median: Mean and median improvement across paired held-out households, every model scored on identical observations.
metric_definitions.per_class_recall: Recall for each state present in the ground truth.
metric_definitions.reporting_delay_minutes: How long after its window a regime's estimate can first be reported: zero online, the lag for a smoother.
metric_definitions.selective_accuracy: Accuracy among only the estimates that committed to a state. Read together with abstention_rate.
metric_definitions.standard_error: Standard deviation of the statistic across household resamples; null with a single household.
metric_definitions.transition: A scored window whose labelled state differs from the labelled state of the window before it. Its episode runs while the following windows keep that labelled state, up to the last scored window; an unlabelled window ends it.

notes: Every setting, estimand and criterion was declared in the protocol before any household was scored.
The record compares inference regimes. Its inference field states the longest lag, which bounds every estimate in it; every cell and comparison in the results carries its own regime.
Every difference is a smoothing gain, available only after the smoother's lag, never an improvement of the online filter.
Every regime is scored on the same labelled windows; the last 12 windows of each recording are not scored, so every smoothed estimate reads its full lag.
Verdicts compare effect sizes and household bootstrap intervals with declared minimal differences; they are not significance tests.
